hypothesis: Does training on a small proportion of model-predicted history, while retaining original gold labels, reduce native greedy repetition and improve coherent continuations?
rationale: Cached FP32 and BF16 generation both repeat; raw numerical failures remain failures. Do not rerun that diagnosis. Previous sequence UL penalized generated repeats; this mechanism instead changes CE conditioning inputs and supplies original gold next-token gradients.

mechanism.prediction: No-gradient clean-context greedy prediction restricted to IDs>=8
mechanism.shift: Prediction at input position j-1 may replace original body input position j
mechanism.boundaries: Preserve input position0, PAD and all original special IDs; no new EOS/BOS or fragment
mechanism.supervision: Every original body/EOS target stays unchanged, supervised exactly once
mechanism.RNG: Dedicated CPU Generator; full state restored with model/AdamW/scheduler/global RNG/sampler
mechanism.objective: Original-gold CE given the mixed history; no UL, contrastive loss, distillation or added head

optimizer: Fresh AdamW lr1e-5/weight_decay0.1; constant scheduler, matching cached CE

budgets.science_budget: Ceil(100M/measured median original teachers per second*1.3+900); plus actual probe must fit total cap
budgets.accounting: Prediction forwards/input positions are additional compute, not teachers; original clean CE input/digest and full sampler match cached CE. Report mixed-input digest and actual replacements separately.

Replaced histories can contradict original gold, especially names/numbers; byte-piece replacements may lack a standalone valid UTF8 rendering. Papers on other tasks do not prove Japanese10M benefit. One seed/mature parent/repeated nonblind DEV. Additional compute differs from cached CE.
